default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-598.title: Dual-EMA cross follow
E-598.hypothesis: A fast EMA crossing a slower one inside the session marks the point where recent buyers or sellers outweigh the earlier ones; late counter-traders get stopped and the move extends.

E-599.title: Lower-high streak break
E-599.hypothesis: After several consecutive lower highs sellers are leaning on every rally; the first close above the last high squeezes them (mirror for higher lows).

E-600.title: Day-open recross after an excursion
E-600.hypothesis: After trading away from the day's open the price closes back through it: the open drive failed and the other side owns the session; follow the recross.

E-601.title: New-extreme count pressure
E-601.hypothesis: When most recent bars keep making higher highs rather than lower lows, participation is one-sided; follow the crossing of that count.

E-602.title: Bollinger re-entry fade
E-602.hypothesis: A close outside the Bollinger band followed by a close back inside shows the stretch was rejected; chasers are trapped and the price reverts toward the mean.

E-603.title: Autocorrelation-regime bar trade
E-603.hypothesis: When consecutive returns have recently been negatively correlated, a big bar overshoots and is faded; when positively correlated, it is followed.

E-604.title: Volatility-normalised drift follow
E-604.hypothesis: A window return large relative to its own noise (t-stat of drift) reflects persistent one-way order flow rather than random jitter; follow when it first crosses.

E-605.title: RSI midline cross follow
E-605.hypothesis: RSI crossing 50 (with an optional dead band) shows average gains overtaking average losses; momentum traders pile in.

E-606.title: Close-range squeeze break
E-606.hypothesis: When the closing-price range of the last window is much narrower than that of four windows, the market is coiled; a close outside it releases stop and breakout orders.

E-607.title: TRIX zero-cross follow
E-607.hypothesis: The slope of a triple-smoothed EMA changing sign filters noise and signals a durable change in direction; follow it.
